name: Question 17
worked_solution:
We need to calculate the product of $1.6$ with itself:

$$
{1.6}^{2}=(1.6)\cdot (1.6)
$$

First, we ignore the decimal points and multiply as if both numbers were whole numbers:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \begin{aligned} &  &  & \,\,\,\,\begin{aligned}\boxed{} \\ \boxed{3}\end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  \\  &  &  & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,\times \,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, \\  &  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,9\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,5\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $16\times 16=256.$

We now count the total number of decimal places in the two factors.

There is $1$ decimal place in the first factor ($1.6$) and $1$ decimal place in the second factor ($1.6$), so their product will have $1+1=2$ decimal places.

We take our value of $256$ and insert a decimal point to make a number with $2$ decimal places:

$$
2\,\overset{↓}{.}\,\,\,{{56}_{⏟}}_{2\text{ digits}}
$$

Therefore, ${1.6}^{2}=2.56\,.$
